_comment: Idea #24 referrer (`sc ref`) — `references[]` NAMES an existing placed ref so the rest of the spec can point at it by `label`. The third sibling of `removals[]` (erase existing) and `overrides[]` (move existing): none of them creates the thing it points at. THIS FILE'S JOB is the EXTERNAL (甲) path + the `anchor` escape hatch (the last references[] entry) — for the clean IN-FILE (乙) path end-to-end, and for the ONLY pattern that actually pins an NPC to ONE SPECIFIC object, read `examples/referrer-chair-anchor.json` instead (that one is the shipped in-game proof, with a control chair). Here: the player placed a chair in-game with `sc pl` (so the exporter emitted it into placements[] with a stable editorId), then aimed at it with `sc ref` and typed a label. ModForge OWNS that object, so build FORCES IT PERSISTENT (0x400 + the cell's Persistent group) — which is exactly what 'a package/alias can target this ref' requires. The label then works in ANY ref field. Coords = the flat Whiterun-stables tundra (ground Z=-4590, same verified spot as scene-export-blacksmith).
_which_slot_you_put_the_label_in_decides: ⚠️ A label gives you a NAME; whether it LOCKS ON TO THAT ONE OBJECT depends on WHICH SLOT you put it in. A package **SingleRef target** slot (sitTarget.target, activate.target, follow.target, patrol.start, escort.target) becomes a `PackageTargetSpecificReference(FormKey)` — the engine acts on THAT REF, no other. A package **location** slot (sandbox.location, travel.place, sleep.location, eat.location) becomes a `LocationTarget` — it anchors an AREA at that ref's position, and the engine then picks whatever furniture/food/bed it likes INSIDE `radius`. So `sandbox.location: "sofia's chair"` does NOT mean 'sit in that chair' — it means 'hang around where that chair is', and she may well sit in a DIFFERENT chair nearby, with NO warning and NO error. For 'she must use THAT object' always use a SingleRef slot (below: sitTarget). This example used to anchor Sofia with `sandbox.location` — it built, it dumped clean, and it could never have proved anything in-game. That is exactly the failure mode this note exists to stop.

npcs.name: Sofia
npcs.greeting: This chair is mine. Find your own.

packages._comment: SitTarget ('walk to and use THAT furniture'). `target` is the LABEL from references[] — that is the whole point of the primitive, and a SingleRef slot is what makes the label bind to ONE REF: build emits `PackageTargetSpecificReference(<the chair's FormKey>)`. No quest alias needed. See the `_which_slot_...` note at the top for why `sandbox.location` is NOT a substitute here.

placements._comment: The chair the player placed in-game with `sc pl`. A plain placement — it is `references[]` that makes it persistent.

references.label: sofia's chair
references.note: she should always come back to this one

references.label: skulvar's hoe
references._comment: The EXTERNAL path, anchor-free: we just NAME a vanilla ref (Skulvar's hoe at the Whiterun stables). Build resolves it in the master link cache, sees it carries no 0x400 flag, and WARNS — the label still resolves, but a quest alias's specific-reference fill or a package SingleRef target may not hold across save/load. Add "anchor": "marker" or "anchor": "replace" (plus base/position/worldspace) to get a persistent anchor of our own.
